correctness.rationale: With q=G/2, d=(gamma1-gamma2)/2, |d|<=q and a,b,G>0, the correct characteristic polynomial is P(s)=(s²+qs+a)(s²+qs+a+2b)-d²s². Its roots all have strictly negative real parts by dissipative energy plus connected positive stiffness. At d=0 the slow normal mode gives R*=G/4-sqrt(max(0,G²/16-a)). For undercritical/critical G, root-sum -G forces spectral abscissa >=-G/4; equality would make P(s-G/4) even but its odd linear coefficient is Gd²/2, hence d=0. For G>4sqrt a, P(-R*)=-d² R*²<0 and P(0)>0 gives a slower real root for imbalance, proving unique balanced optimum for all G. R*(G) increases up to G=4sqrt a then decreases; global max sqrt a. At noncritical simple modes implicit roots yield quadratic imbalance costs G/(8b)d² and R*²/(2b sqrt(G²/4-4a))d²; at the critical double low mode 2b(δs)²=ad² yields sqrt(a/(2b))|d|. Independent SymPy exact polynomial and shifted coefficient and 18 numerical root diagnostics across all regimes passed. The rate is spectral asymptotic exponent, not a uniform norm bound at defective eigenvalues.
